instructions: Slice the tops off the 4 tomatoes and keep them as lids. Scoop the insides into a bowl with a spoon, leaving a wall about 1/4 inch thick so they don't collapse in the oven.
Slice the tops off the 4 peppers and keep them too. Pull out the seeds and white ribs.
Stand the tomatoes and peppers in a large baking dish. Sprinkle the insides with 1/4 tsp of the salt and a pinch of the sugar, and put a small piece of the 1 tbsp butter in the bottom of each one.
Blend or mash the tomato insides with 1/4 cup of the olive oil, the 1 tbsp tomato paste, the rest of the 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Set this sauce aside.
Finely chop the onion and the 2 garlic cloves. Cut the zucchini into small cubes. Finely chop 1/2 cup of the parsley and 1/4 cup of the mint.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium. Add the onion and cook for about 5 minutes, until it's soft and see-through.
Add the zucchini and cook for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Stir in the 1 cup rice and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the edges of the grains turn see-through.

Pour in half the can of tomatoes, 3/4 cup water, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the last 1/4 tsp pepper. Bring it to a boil and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then. The rice will still be firm. Take it off the heat and stir in the parsley and mint.
Spoon the filling into the tomatoes and peppers so they're about two thirds full. The rice swells as it bakes. Spoon a little of the sauce into each one to top it up, then put the lids on.
Peel the 3 potatoes and cut them into wedges. Tuck them into the gaps around the vegetables and sprinkle them with the last 1/2 tsp salt.
Pour the rest of the sauce, the rest of the can of tomatoes and 1 1/2 cups water into the dish around the vegetables. Drizzle the last 2 tbsp olive oil over everything.
Cover the dish with foil and bake for 35 minutes.

Take off the foil and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the potatoes are tender, the tops of the vegetables are browned at the edges and the rice is soft when you taste a spoonful. If the dish looks dry, add a splash of water.
Taste the rice. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the vegetables.
Let them sit for 10 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature with slices of the feta.
method_notes: Both hollow out tomatoes and peppers, keep the tops as lids, use the tomato insides as the sauce, and fill them with short grain rice cooked briefly with onion, garlic and fresh herbs so it finishes in the oven. My Greek Dish adds zucchini and eggplant to the filling, puts a little butter, salt and sugar inside each vegetable, tucks potato wedges around them and bakes at 350°F covered then uncovered, with ground beef as an option. Super Golden Bakes uses dill, pine nuts and dried cranberries, a lot more olive oil, and bakes longer at 400°F. This one follows My Greek Dish with tomatoes and peppers only and no meat.
